theme: Prediction markets and betting data: Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold APIs and datasets on earnings and travel/regulation events

candidates.name: prediction-market-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Framework + released dataset described as 'the largest publicly available dataset of Polymarket and Kalshi market and trade data'. Parquet-based storage: Kalshi/{markets,trades}, Polymarket/{blocks,markets,trades}. A pre-collected 36GB compressed archive (data.tar.zst) is offered via Cloudflare R2 download. MIT licensed, 3.8k stars/541 forks, 30 commits on main. Not filtered to any single event category — covers all Polymarket/Kalshi markets and trades, so earnings, macro, travel and regulation contracts (e.g. any 'will ABNB report X', CPI/travel-demand-adjacent markets, hurricane/weather markets) would be included wherever they were listed on either venue.
candidates.why_useful: Point-in-time market/trade-level data (order-level, timestamped) is exactly the kind of vintage series gap #4 calls for; could be filtered for ABNB-earnings contracts, travel-shock markets (hurricanes, World Cup 2026), or regulatory-event contracts (STR ordinances, FTC/DOJ actions) if such markets existed on Kalshi/Polymarket historically. Also usable as a general market-implied-probability cross-check for event studies (gap #11, #12).
candidates.time_coverage: Full available Polymarket/Kalshi trade history up to repo's collection date (exact start not confirmed from README excerpt)
candidates.size_hint: 36GB compressed (data.tar.zst); Parquet files, additional CSV/JSON/PNG/PDF analysis outputs
candidates.last_activity: 30 commits on main, exact date not shown in fetched excerpt

candidates.name: forecasting
candidates.what_it_holds: Git-scraping repo (GitHub Actions workflows commit periodic snapshots) tracking forecasting/prediction-market state over time across at least five platforms with per-platform folders: Kalshi, Manifold Markets, Metaculus, Polymarket, ForecastEx. Small repo (8 stars, 1 fork, 54 commits); no license or description text was visible.
candidates.why_useful: Because it is git-scraped, each commit is a genuine point-in-time snapshot recoverable via `git log`/`git show` on the tracked files — directly matches the point-in-time/vintage-series gap (#4) for prediction-market-implied probabilities on earnings, elections, or macro releases, without needing to run a scraper against a live API. Could plausibly include ABNB-relevant contracts (earnings surprise markets, CPI, Fed decisions used as macro backdrop) as of each snapshot date.
candidates.time_coverage: Since first workflow run; span not confirmed from fetched content (54 total commits, so likely a shorter/thinner history)
candidates.size_hint: Small repo; likely markdown/JSON/CSV snapshot files per run
candidates.last_activity: 54 commits on main; date not shown

candidates.name: polyledger
candidates.what_it_holds: Self-hosted Polymarket indexer that streams on-chain OrderFilled events from Polygon via Envio HyperSync plus CLOB API market metadata into a single queryable DuckDB file ('one file on disk', SQL-queryable). No committed/downloadable dataset — user must run the backfill themselves (a few hours to a couple of days on free tier). MIT licensed, 22 commits, example output timestamped 2026-09-02 suggesting active/recent.
candidates.why_useful: A one-command / scriptable method to build a full point-in-time Polymarket trade ledger (all categories) in a DuckDB file the team already uses elsewhere in its stack — lower effort than writing a custom indexer if the team wants an on-chain-verified, timestamped record of Polymarket odds around ABNB earnings or travel/regulation events.
candidates.time_coverage: Full Polymarket on-chain history back to inception once backfilled
candidates.size_hint: Not stated; scales with full Polymarket trade history

candidates.name: pmxt
candidates.what_it_holds: "CCXT for prediction markets": a unified Python/TypeScript SDK, hosted API, self-hostable server, CLI, and MCP integration that normalizes access across Polymarket, Polymarket US, Kalshi, Limitless, Probable, Baozi, Myriad, Opinion, Metaculus, Smarkets, Hyperliquid, Gemini Titan, SuiBets, Rain, and Hunch. MIT licensed, 2.1k stars/269 forks, 1,687 commits, actively developed.
candidates.why_useful: One client library to pull current AND (via each venue's own history endpoints) historical market data across a dozen-plus prediction-market venues including Metaculus, rather than writing bespoke API clients per platform — useful if the team wants to pull ABNB-earnings or travel/regulation contracts across multiple venues with one interface.
candidates.time_coverage: N/A (live API wrapper; historical depth depends on underlying venue APIs)
candidates.last_activity: 1,687 commits, actively maintained as of fetch

candidates.name: Awesome-Prediction-Market-Tools

candidates.name: metaforecast (now in Squiggle monorepo, apps/metaforecast)
candidates.what_it_holds: Aggregator that fetches and indexes forecasts/questions from Metaculus, Manifold Markets, and other platforms into a searchable Postgres database with a GraphQL API and a manualDownload.js script; no committed data files or DB dump in-repo. Archived (read-only) since 7 Mar 2025; source moved to the Squiggle monorepo (apps/metaforecast). MIT licensed, 622 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A cross-platform question/forecast search index (GraphQL) spanning Metaculus + Manifold (and historically other venues) that could surface ABNB-earnings, travel-demand, or STR-regulation questions without hand-querying each platform's own API; the manualDownload script is a plausible one-command pull method even though the hosted DB itself is not archived in-repo.
candidates.time_coverage: Active period of the aggregator; archived Mar 2025
candidates.last_activity: Archived 7 Mar 2025 (622 commits); superseded by Squiggle monorepo

notes: This session's shared WebSearch tool budget was already exhausted (200/200) before I could run a single query, so this scout is built entirely on WebFetch against github.com/topics/*, github.com/search, huggingface.co, and direct repo URLs recalled from training knowledge. github.com/search (the real search endpoint) returned HTTP 429 with Retry-After 3600 after a couple of calls, and github.com/topics/<tag> pages intermittently 404'd or rate-limited on repeat hits — topics/kalshi, topics/predictit and topics/metaculus worked and were the most productive single calls (each returned ~10-21 repos in one shot). No repo found is specifically built around ABNB, earnings-call markets, or STR/travel regulation as a first-class category; PredictIt topic results were entirely US-politics-focused and excluded as off-theme (no data files, no relevance). The most promising finds are general-purpose Polymarket/Kalshi market-and-trade archives (Jon-Becker/prediction-market-analysis) and a git-scraped multi-platform snapshot repo (PatMyron/forecasting) that would need to be filtered post-hoc for any ABNB-relevant, travel-demand, or STR-regulation contracts — I did not find evidence such contracts exist on Kalshi/Polymarket in volume, so the practical value is likely as a general point-in-time/vintage-series and market-implied-probability method rather than a direct ABNB data source. Recommend a future scout retry github.com/search and github.com/topics pages once the per-IP rate limit clears (looked like ~1 hour cooldown), and specifically try queries combining 'kalshi' with 'CPI', 'jobs report', 'travel', 'tourism', or 'hurricane' once search capacity is available, since none of the topic-page listings surfaced anything travel/earnings-specific despite those being real Kalshi market categories.
